text:
This page applies to:

developments that need planning permission

nationally significant infrastructure projects (NSIPs) with applications submitted on or after 2 November 2026

If you need to create or enhance habitat as part of your development, there are rules about how you may be able to count this towards your biodiversity net gain (BNG). These rules make sure that BNG delivers actions beyond what is already required through statutory obligations or policies.

There are habitat schemes and activities that you can:

count in full

count up to no net loss

not count at all

How these schemes and activities can count towards your BNG depends on whether you create these habitats as:

mitigation and compensation actions for other impacts

enhancing actions

The same rules on what you can count apply across both on-site and off-site BNG. However, any off-site habitat creation and enhancement must be registered on the biodiversity gain sites register for it to count towards your BNG.

Special rules apply to delivering BNG on protected sites. Protected sites are areas that have a high level of legal and policy protection because of their natural and cultural importance. You should avoid impacts to protected sites wherever possible.

What you can count in full

You may be able to count in full enhancing activities delivered to comply with certain statutory obligations or policies. For example:

green infrastructure

river basin management plan (RBMP) enhancement

sustainable drainage systems (SuDS)

You can satisfy all of your BNG through these enhancing activities, including up to no net loss as well as your 10% net gain (or more where applicable).

Enhancing protected sites for BNG purposes

You may want to carry out enhancing activities within a protected site to contribute to your BNG. You can count these activities in full towards your BNG if both the following conditions apply:

you do not carry out these enhancing activities for other statutory obligations

there are no adverse impacts on the protected site

Before you can enhance habitat within a protected site, you must:

get agreement from the consenting body

make sure that any protected species licences required are in place

You must adhere to the following rules to provide enhancements within a protected site:

terrestrial protected sites – you can enhance the non-designated features of the protected site provided that there are no adverse impacts on the protected site

intertidal protected sites – you can enhance any intertidal habitat on a protected site, including any designated features

What you can count up to no net loss

If you are carrying out habitat mitigation or compensation activities required through statutory obligations or policies, some of these can only count up to no net loss. Your additional 10% net gain above no net loss must come from separate activities other than mitigation and compensation.

Activities that count up to no net loss include:

nutrient neutrality or mitigation

mitigation or compensation to protected species or protected sites

river basin management plan (RBMP) mitigation

suitable alternative natural green space (SANG)

environmental impact assessment mitigation

mitigation or compensation to functionally linked land (FLL)

district level licensing schemes

sustainable drainage systems (SuDS) – when part of nutrient neutrality

Mitigation or compensation to protected sites

You may enhance habitats within a protected site as mitigation or compensation for other statutory obligations or policies, if agreed with the consenting body.

Any mitigation or compensation for impacts on protected sites can only count up to no net loss. You will need to deliver additional measures to meet your net gain.

Example

Your development has a baseline biodiversity value of 10 units. The development works will result in the loss of habitats equivalent to 5 biodiversity units.

In addition, you need to do habitat creation to mitigate for impacts the development will have on a nearby protected site (for example, provide SANG). These works create 6 biodiversity units but, because this is mitigation activity that must be agreed with the consenting authority, you can only count 5 of these units. This will bring your total back to 10 units, giving you the equivalent of no net loss.

You must therefore deliver an additional 1 unit to achieve your 10% BNG. This unit must come from habitat creation or enhancement activities specifically for the purpose of BNG, or from those activities that can count in full. This can include additional habitat enhancement works on the mitigation site itself, other on-site or off-site gains, or the purchase of statutory biodiversity credits.

To count mitigation or compensation to protected sites towards your BNG, you must adhere to the following rules:

terrestrial protected sites – you can only enhance the non-designated features of the protected site, provided that there are no adverse impacts on the protected site

intertidal protected sites – you can enhance any intertidal habitat on a protected site, including any designated features

What does not count at all

You cannot include some habitat activities towards your BNG at all. For example:

restocking conditions relating to a tree felling licence or a restocking notice

remediation under the environmental damage regulations

remedial habitat creation or enhancement carried out under an existing planning obligation or condition such as a landfill restoration plan

How to include other activities in your BNG

To count other habitat creation or enhancement activities towards your BNG, you must include them in your:

metric calculation

biodiversity gain plan – for developments that need planning permission

outline and updated or phase biodiversity gain plans – for NSIPs

If you are counting work for another activity in part towards your BNG, you should enter it into your metric calculation like any other habitat creation or enhancement work. You should also explain clearly in your biodiversity gain plan how at least 10% of your BNG is coming from habitat creation or enhancement outside the activity.
